stories.headline: Blue Jays' Spencer Miles: Stellar showing in latest short start
stories.detail: Miles struck out four and allowed two hits and no walks over three scoreless frames in a start during last Sunday's 7-2 win over the Rangers. Drawing his eighth start of the season, Miles was sharp but was limited to 46 pitches since he's been mostly used in a relief role since the All-Star break. The Blue Jays haven't used Miles since last weekend, but he could be a candidate to pitch multiple innings in bulk relief in one of the team's final two games of the season against the Reds. The Blue Jays have named Trey Yesavage and Max Scherzer as their starters for Saturday and Sunday, respectively, and both are likely to be operating with limited workloads.

stories.headline: Rangers' Gavin Collyer: Optioned to minors
stories.detail: The Rangers optioned Collyer to the Arizona Complex League on Saturday. Collyer gave up two earned runs in two innings during Friday's contest and will now be pushed out of Texas' bullpen in favor of Robby Ahlstrom, who will give the team another fresh arm to work with.

stories.headline: Rangers' Robby Ahlstrom: Up from Triple-A
stories.detail: The Rangers recalled Ahlstrom from Triple-A Round Rock on Saturday. The 27-year-old will provide the Rangers with another fresh bullpen arm to work with, replacing Gavin Collyer. Ahlstrom has recorded a 6.08 ERA and 1.43 WHIP over 37 innings with the Rangers this year and will likely be limited to middle-relief duty.

stories.headline: Rangers' Logan O'Hoppe: Up from Round Rock
stories.detail: The Rangers recalled O'Hoppe from Triple-A Round Rock on Saturday. O'Hoppe will rejoin the Rangers for the final weekend of the regular season to give the team a bat to replace Josh Jung, who landed on the IL with a fractured hand Saturday. O'Hoppe has posted just a .578 OPS in 274 plate appearances in the big leagues this year and isn't likely to see much playing time to close out the season.

stories.headline: Rangers' Josh Jung: Placed on IL
stories.detail: The Rangers placed Jung on the 10-day injured list Saturday with a fractured right hand. Jung's move to the injured list will officially rule him out for the rest of the regular season and the start of a potential postseason run, though it's more likely that he remains sidelined until 2027. Cody Freeman and Nicky Lopez are the leading candidates to pick up starts in the infield while Jung is out, and Logan O'Hoppe will come up from Triple-A to replenish Texas' bench depth.

stories.headline: Pirates' Oneil Cruz: Exits early Saturday
stories.detail: Cruz was removed from Saturday's game against the Tigers due to an apparent injury, Dominic Campbell of SI.com reports. Cruz's knee seemed to be bothering him after his foot got stuck in the grass while he made a sliding catch in the first inning, and he was eventually taken out of the game in the third. The Pirates should provide more information on his status in the near future, but with just one game left on the schedule after Saturday, Pittsburgh may opt to keep him on the sidelines no matter what.

stories.headline: Blue Jays' Max Scherzer: Starting Sunday
stories.detail: Scherzer will start Sunday's regular-season finale against the Reds, Ben Nicholson-Smith of Sportsnet.ca reports. Scherzer said that he's still undecided about whether he'll retire after this season, but he'll officially get to make at least one more start on a big-league mound before he hangs up his cleats. The 42-year-old hasn't been particularly effective this season, posting a 6.14 ERA and 1.36 WHIP across 77.2 innings, but facing a Reds offense that's turned in a .690 OPS since the beginning of September could allow him to end his Hall of Fame career on a high note.

stories.headline: Marlins' Kyle Stowers: Battling abdominal injury
stories.detail: Stowers isn't in the lineup for Saturday's game against Atlanta due to an abdominal injury, Daniel Alvarez-Montes of ElExtraBase.com reports. Saturday will mark the third consecutive game that Stowers hasn't started as he battles abdominal pain, and with the Marlins ' season set to end Sunday, the team may decide to keep him out as a precaution. Stowers' absence Saturday will allow Deyvison De Los Santos to start at first base.

stories.headline: Giants' Bo Davidson: Singles in loss
stories.detail: Davidson went 1-for-3 in Friday's 2-0 loss to the Dodgers. Davidson hit a single in the seventh inning, accounting for one of San Francisco's three hits Friday. He's recorded a hit in each of his first four big-league games, slashing .308/.357/.308 with two runs scored and a stolen base in 14 plate appearances. The 24-year-old figures to continue receiving regular opportunities over the Giants ' final two games of the year.

stories.headline: Giants' Sam Hentges: Logs scoreless inning Friday
stories.detail: Hentges threw a scoreless inning while striking out one in Friday's 2-0 loss to the Dodgers. Hentges recorded his third straight scoreless outing while throwing eight of his 11 pitches for strikes. The 30-year-old southpaw has been productive of late, turning in a 1.69 ERA and 6:2 K:BB in 5.1 innings over his last six appearances. On the campaign, he owns a 3.28 ERA, 1.65 WHIP and 39:25 K:BB in 35.2 innings across 44 outings.
